Python's csv module quotes only fields that contain ',', '"', CR or LF, so 'x;=1+1;y' is written unquoted. A value with an embedded line break ('x\n=1+1') is quoted for comma readers, but a ';' reader does not honor a quote that is not at the start of its piece (the new test fails on the alpha with the cells [..., 'x', '=1+1', 'y,10.0.0.5,...']). IPv6 scope IDs carry the same text into src_ip/dst_ip: ipaddress accepted 'fe80::1%x;=1+1;y'. This is a simulation only: no spreadsheet app is installed here, and I installed none. The input path is imported Zeek logs; I did not test whether a capture can carry ';=' into a CSV cell.

rows.defense: check_content_length() refuses a Content-Length above MAXGUARD_MAX_UPLOAD_MB + 64 KiB before the body is read. save_upload() counts bytes while it copies the already-parsed upload into data/uploads/, then deletes the partial file. suffix_for() picks .pcap/.zip/.tar.gz from the first bytes; anything else gets no suffix, so the pipeline refuses it with 400. findings.evidence: Chunked 30 MiB with a 1 MiB limit: 'sent 30 MiB: server tmp= 30.0 MiB rss=101384 KiB answered_yet=no', then 'reply after 4.29s: HTTP/1.1 413'. Ingest app with the token: 'sent 30 MiB: server tmp= 30.0 MiB ... answered_yet=no', 413 after 4.28s. POST /mode: 'server temp file = 30.0 MiB', answer '303 See Other'. PATCH /alerts/{id}/status: 30.0 MiB, then 400. PATCH /api/alerts/{id} with 200 MiB JSON: VmHWM 90 -> 1026 MiB, '422'. 'Content-Length: 100' + 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' passes check_content_length and reaches the app (log 'Expected boundary character 45...'). Cause: app.py:282-286 reads only the header. app.py:253/265 then call request.form(), and Starlette appends file parts with no cap (formparsers.py:191; only non-file parts are capped, at :187), writing every chunk (:286) to a SpooledTemporaryFile (:233) that rolls to an unnamed file in TMPDIR. save_upload() (app.py:327-345) counts only afterwards, while copying. web/routes.py:147 and :195 call request.form() with no checks, and FastAPI keeps JSON bodies in memory. ARCHITECTURE.md:772-774 says the copy-time check covers 'a client can leave the header out'. The test tests/unit/test_api.py:144-153 calls save_upload() directly, so it cannot see this. Alpha exposure: local processes only (cross-site requests get 403 before the body is read). Spring: ingest-token holders on port 8001.
findings.fix:
Count body bytes as they arrive, for every request, in a small ASGI middleware in new_app(). It sits under TrustedHost and the cross-site check, so both apps get it. Uploads may use MAXGUARD_MAX_UPLOAD_MB + 64 KiB; any other body may use 1 MiB.
+UPLOAD_PATHS = {"/api/analyses", "/api/ingest"}
+SMALL_BODY_BYTES = MIB
...
+    app.add_middleware(BodyLimit)
     app.middleware("http")(refuse_cross_site_changes)
...
+class BodyLimit:
+    def __init__(self, app):
+        self.app = app
+    async def __call__(self, scope, receive, send):
+        if scope["type"] != "http":
+            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
+            return
+        app = scope["app"]
+        if scope["path"] in UPLOAD_PATHS:
+            limit, detail = app.state.max_upload_bytes + FORM_OVERHEAD_BYTES, too_large_message(app)
+        else:
+            limit, detail = SMALL_BODY_BYTES, "request body larger than 1 MB"
+        received = 0
+        async def counting_receive():
+            nonlocal received
+            message = await receive()
+            received += len(message.get("body", b""))
+            if received > limit:
+                raise HTTPException(413, detail)
+            return message
+        await self.app(scope, counting_receive, send)
The full diff with 3 regression tests is at $W/fix-body-limit-with-tests.diff. The tests drive the ASGI app with a chunked body and assert 413 and bytes pulled <= limit. All 3 fail on the current code (pulled 8388688; 422; 303) and pass with the fix. Verified: alpha unit tests 546 passed, 1 skipped (543+3); ALL unit tests 874 passed, 1 skipped (871+3); integration upload test passes in zeek/zeek:9.0.0. Live on :18739: chunked 30 MiB -> 413 before 5 MiB, temp 0.0 MiB; POST /mode 30 MiB -> 413, temp 0.0 MiB; 200 MiB JSON -> 413 in 0.4s, VmHWM 97 -> 97 MiB. Normal upload, small chunked upload, ingest, PATCH JSON, PATCH form and /mode still return 200/200/200/200/200/303. Then change ARCHITECTURE.md:772-774 to say the size is counted as the body arrives. A narrower fix that only wraps request.receive in the two upload routes is at $W/fix-chunked-upload.diff (verified: 544 passed; 30 MiB chunked -> 413 before 5 MiB). It leaves /mode and the JSON routes open. Optional, verified: add 'Connection: close' to the early 401/404/413 so uvicorn stops receiving.

BYPASS found (E): a file literally named 'images.tar.part-aa<LF>x' passes require_listed because find_parts globs images.tar.part-* and `grep -Fxq -- "$file"` is handed a two-line pattern whose first line ('images.tar.part-aa') matches the listed part; verify_checksums --strict never checks the unlisted file; its bytes were streamed into `docker load` (injected marker landed at offset 1000 of the loaded 2436-byte stream). findings.title: install.sh require_listed can be bypassed by an unlisted bundle file whose name contains a newline, streaming it into docker load
findings.repro: Build a fake bundle with scripts/build-offline-bundle.sh (fake docker, PART_BYTES=1000); then: printf 'INJECTED' > "dist/images.tar.part-aa$(printf '\n')x"; (cd dist && MAXGUARD_SKIP_START=1 bash install.sh); grep -c INJECTED loaded-images.bin  -> 1.
findings.evidence: require_listed() (scripts/install.sh:77-89) does `for f in "${PARTS[@]}"; do grep -Fxq -- "$f" <<<"$listed"`. find_parts globs images.tar.part-* so a file named 'images.tar.part-aa\nx' is included; passing that two-line string to grep -Fx makes grep match if EITHER line ('images.tar.part-aa', which IS listed) matches, so the check passes. verify_checksums `sha256 -c --strict` (install.sh:50) only checks listed files, so it never inspects the extra file. stream_bundle_file then cats it into `docker load` (install.sh:100); in my run the injected marker appeared at offset 1000 of the loaded stream. A newline in a filename is invalid on the documented FAT32/exFAT USB medium, and an attacker able to fully tamper the bundle can already rewrite the still-unsigned SHA256SUMS, so impact is limited to the POSIX-filesystem, add-only case; it is a correctness gap in the 'refuses unlisted files' guarantee.
findings.fix: In require_listed, reject any part name containing a control char before matching, e.g. `case $file in *$'\n'*) die "$file: illegal name";; esac`, or match NUL-safely: build the listed set from SHA256SUMS and compare with `[[ " $listed_nul " == ... ]]` using a delimiter that cannot appear in names. Signing SHA256SUMS with the JAI-08 key (the acknowledged open item) also closes this.

## AHM-04 step 2 — dependency scans and upstream release/CVE review (sec-repo)

All scans run with the project-approved tools only; **nothing was installed, pulled or downloaded** (the computed task forbids it, and the user's "I'll approve before installing" request never triggered: every tool needed — pip-audit 2.10.1, bandit 1.9.4, actionlint 1.7.12, gitleaks v8.30.1, shellcheck v0.11.0, docker images — was already present and approved). The only blocked capability was the GitHub REST API (proxy 403 for api.github.com/repos/zeek|OISF|ollama); I worked around it read-only with `git ls-remote` and WebFetch of raw.githubusercontent.com/github.com, and could not reach `suricata.io`/`forum.suricata.io` (DNS ENOTFOUND via the proxy) or OSV (`api.osv.dev` 403).

### (a) Security tooling

**pip-audit 2.10.1** on the exact installed set of `ref/.venv` (`pip freeze --all` → 39 pkgs → `pip-audit -r`, PyPI service; OSV service was unreachable). 6 vulns in 3 packages:

```
Name              Version   ID                  Fix Versions
certifi           2026.7.22 PYSEC-2026-4320     2026.10.18   (GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2)
opentelemetry-api 1.45.0    CVE-2026-114603     1.45.1       (GHSA-xcq7-p3pf-p88h)
setuptools        79.0.1    PYSEC-2026-3447     83.0.0       (CVE-2026-59890, GHSA-h35f-9h28-mq5c)
setuptools        79.0.1    GHSA-xmj3-9gf7-h52w 84.1.0
```

Which matter for MaxGuard:
- **certifi 2026.7.22 → 2026.10.18 (PYSEC-2026-4320): the one worth acting on.** The bundled CA store still trusts `emSign ECC Root CA - G3`, whose chained eMudhra intermediates have compromised, revoked keys — an on-path attacker could present valid-looking certs. certifi is a **shipped runtime** dep (via requests). MaxGuard runs offline and only talks to the local Ollama over plain HTTP, so real exposure is low, **but** the sensor shipper and the OPNsense enforcer do make outbound TLS (`ca_file`, `MAXGUARD_OPNSENSE_CA`). Bump the pin to `certifi>=2026.10.18` and rebuild the bundle before release.
- **opentelemetry-api 1.45.0 (CVE-2026-114603): not exploitable here.** ReDoS in `TraceState.from_header`; it is pulled in by FastAPI as API-only (no SDK/exporter, confirmed in DEPENDENCIES.md §8) and MaxGuard never parses a W3C `tracestate` header, so nothing reaches the vulnerable path. Bump opportunistically.
- **setuptools 79.0.1 (two issues): build-time only, not shipped at runtime.** One is sdist `MANIFEST.in` Unicode-normalization bypass on macOS, the other a Windows legacy-wheel-install path escape. setuptools is venv/build tooling, not in the 8 runtime deps. Low relevance; update the build venv when convenient.
- `pip` not flagged.

**bandit 1.9.4** `-r maxguard -q` on the ALL build: 16 results, all expected / false positives for a tool that shells out to Zeek/Suricata and parses hostile captures:
- `B202 tarfile_unsafe_members` HIGH at `adapters/zeeklogs.py:100` — **false positive**: the call is `t.extractall(dest, filter="data")`, which is exactly the row-1 defense (bandit doesn't recognise the filter kwarg).
- `B608 hardcoded_sql` MEDIUM ×3 (`response/approvals.py:116,220`, `storage/events.py:120`) — **false positives**: the only interpolated tokens are internal constants (`OPEN_STATES`, column names, `COLUMNS`); every caller value is a `?`/`$` bind parameter.
- `B104 bind_all_interfaces` MEDIUM ×3 (`decoy/__main__.py:22`, `decoy/service.py:124,137`) — **expected**: a decoy is meant to listen on its own IP/container (CLAUDE.md rule 5).
- `B404`/`B603` subprocess ×9 LOW — **expected**: Zeek/Suricata are launched as argv lists, no shell.

**gitleaks v8.30.1** `git /repo --redact` over full history: 8 leaks → 5 real duplicates of the one legacy OpenRouter key + 3 false positives (see finding sec-13a and row 13). `detect` on the ALL build: 1 hit = the `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----` literal in `tests/unit/test_signing.py:26` (an assertion, not a key).

**ShellCheck v0.11.0** on all 5 shell scripts in the ALL build: build-offline-bundle.sh, install.sh, live_check.sh, uninstall.sh = **clean (exit 0)**; make_fixtures.sh = one `SC2012` info note (`ls` in a `$(...)`, KAR-02), not a security issue.

**actionlint 1.7.12** (`-shellcheck`) on both workflows: **0 errors**.

### (b) Upstream releases & CVEs since the pinned versions (as of 2026-10-27)

**Zeek — pinned 9.0.0 → newest stable 9.0.1** (released 2026-10-26; 9.1.0 is dev-only, `v9.1.0` has no release/NEWS, only `v9.1.0-dev`). **9.0.1 is a large security release: 48 advisories (35 HIGH + 13 MEDIUM), GHSA IDs only, no CVEs assigned.** Mostly protocol-parser memory-exhaustion / DoS on attacker-controlled traffic — directly in MaxGuard's threat surface (it feeds hostile pcaps to Zeek). Notables: **ZIP: Unbounded decompression** [GHSA-2prm-q48h-m96w](https://github.com/zeek/zeek/security/advisories/GHSA-2prm-q48h-m96w) (HIGH, patched 9.0.1 — relevant to the row-1 archive threat), SSL unbounded cert state [GHSA-rmv9-rq35-fw28], TLS unbounded extensions [GHSA-j2wq-86vc-93cg], QUIC eager allocation [GHSA-5695-9qhq-wmmj], X509/OCSP unbounded growth [GHSA-vhc3-782q-hqjj], RDP many small x509 certs [GHSA-x38g-wp8h-rfrf], TCP reassembly overlap [GHSA-5xxm-w466-8ghx], zip use-after-free from gzip multipart [GHSA-7cf3-cq69-g7p6]. Plus a WebSocket fd-inheritance bug fix. Recommend bumping the engine + sensor base image to `zeek/zeek:9.0.1`.
Source: [Zeek 9.0.1 NEWS](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zeek/zeek/v9.0.1/NEWS) · release page https://github.com/zeek/zeek/releases/tag/v9.0.1 (HTML 403 to me; NEWS verified via raw). 45 GHSA IDs enumerated in NEWS; I spot-verified GHSA-2prm-q48h-m96w (HIGH, affected ≤8.0.9/≤8.2.1, patched 8.0.11 & 9.0.1, 2026-10-26).

**Suricata — engine 7.0.10 (Debian 13) → newest 7.0.17 (2026-07-07); sensor 8.0.7 is current (no newer 8.0.x; no 9.x).** The **engine's 7.0.10 is behind by seven patch releases (7.0.11–7.0.17) carrying 37 Security entries / 33 distinct CVEs**, several CRITICAL, all on the parsing path MaxGuard exercises:
- CVE-2026-45764 (CRITICAL) http2 type confusion → crash/DoS; fixed 7.0.16 & 8.0.5
- CVE-2026-45766 (CRITICAL) nfs OOM; CVE-2026-45769 (CRITICAL) ikev2 OOM; CVE-2026-31935 (CRITICAL) unbounded http2 frames; CVE-2026-22258 (CRITICAL) dcerpc fragment buffering OOM (7.0.14)
- plus HIGH: CVE-2026-57227/57228 (mqtt/mime, 7.0.17), CVE-2026-46387/45767/45759/45762/45765/45747 (7.0.16), CVE-2026-31933/31932/31937 (7.0.15), CVE-2026-22259/22264/22262 (7.0.14), CVE-2025-64344/64333 (7.0.13), CVE-2025-59147 (7.0.12), CVE-2025-53537/53538 (7.0.11), and more.
**Caveat:** the engine installs Suricata from the Debian 13 `suricata` package, and Debian commonly **backports** security fixes into its `1:7.0.10-…` package without bumping the upstream version — so the Debian build may already carry some of these. This could not be verified here (Debian sites blocked; apt needs network). Verify on a built image: `dpkg -l suricata`, `zcat /usr/share/doc/suricata/changelog.Debian.gz`, and the [Debian security tracker](https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/source-package/suricata). Otherwise prefer pinning the engine to a current Suricata (e.g. install 8.0.7 from trixie-backports, or move to the `jasonish/suricata:8.0.7` build for the engine too).
Source (authoritative): [Suricata 7.0.17 ChangeLog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OISF/suricata/suricata-7.0.17/ChangeLog). `suricata.io`/`forum.suricata.io` were unreachable (DNS); cross-checks: [CVE-2026-45764 (Debian tracker)](https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-45764), advisory GHSA-5rvq-72r5-rqhr.

**Ollama — pinned 0.35.1 → newest stable 0.40.11** (0.40.12-rc1 pre-release, 2026-10-27). I found **no advisory naming 0.36–0.40 as a fix version**, and the most recent Ollama CVEs are already fixed at or below the pin: path traversal in `/api/pull` [CVE-2026-103663] fixed in **0.35.0**, SSRF [CVE-2026-108836] fixed in **0.34.2**, GGUF OOB read "Bleeding Llama" [CVE-2026-7482] fixed in 0.17.1. So **0.35.1 is not known-vulnerable** to the current public Ollama CVEs. Extra mitigation already in place: `docker/compose.yaml` puts Ollama on the `ai` network with `internal: true` (no route out) and MAXGUARD_OFFLINE guards the engine, so even the pull/SSRF classes are not reachable from off-host. Upgrading is optional (features/perf), not a security must. Could not confirm per-release notes for 0.36–0.39 (not shown on the releases page; GitHub API blocked).
Sources: [Ollama releases](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases) · [CVE-2026-103663 (Mend)](https://www.mend.io/vulnerability-database/CVE-2026-103663/) · [CVE-2026-108836 (Debian)](https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-108836) · [Bleeding Llama CVE-2026-7482](https://docs.indusface.com/en/article/19558641-3fc7-4243-9509-88fd8c59d532) · [osv.dev](https://osv.dev/vulnerability/CLEANSTART-2026-WE49959).

### Image-digest note (relates to row 16)
docs/DEPENDENCIES.md records `jasonish/suricata:8.0.7@sha256:7ca2546f…` but the image pulled in this environment is `@sha256:bf4bea5b45d9…` (a different/single-arch digest), and the compose files pin maxguard/ollama/suricata/zeek by **tag**, not digest, despite §3 recommending digest pins. Not a row-16 failure (the row doesn't claim digest pinning), but worth reconciling before release so "what we ship" is reproducible.

### Notes on scope / method
Rows 14 and 15 describe W6 (JAI-09, JON-05) artifacts that post-date the exact AHM-04 (W5) snapshot, so they were tested in the ALL build; they are Fall-2026 alpha-release deliverables, hence `in_alpha=true`. All attacks were run locally in private build copies under /tmp scratch, against a fake `docker` and TestClient on 127.0.0.1 with synthetic data — no outside host was contacted, no real secret was created or printed (every secret/email/IP is redacted above).

I reproduced how the file splits, but the defect itself is not demonstrated.

What I reproduced: my own ssl.log, with cipher 'TLS_RSA_WITH_NULL_SHA x;=1+1;y', put through the alpha CLI gives a CSV with no formula-start cell when read with ','. Read with csv.reader(delimiter=';'), it gives two '=1+1' cells. The proposed fix removes them in this simulation and keeps the suite green.

Why I did not confirm it:

(1) No traffic path in the alpha. The CSV columns (report.py:32-38) carry no `details`. Every title is a fixed string except 'Weak cipher {cipher}' (rules/tls.py:29) and the integer key length. Zeek 9.0.0 fills the cipher from a lookup table: base/protocols/ssl/main.zeek:305 `c$ssl$cipher = cipher_desc[cipher];`, and unknown codes become 'unknown-%d' (consts.zeek). So a capture cannot put ';' or '=' into that cell. Zeek-written addresses carry no IPv6 scope IDs. Only a hand-written log archive that the user chooses to import can deliver the payload. The CSV export exists only in the CLI (cli/main.py:136 is the only caller of to_csv).

(2) The code does exactly what the documented defense says. ARCHITECTURE.md:1070: "A CSV cell that starts with =, +, -, @, a tab, or a line break gets a leading '". Read as the comma file it is, the CSV is clean.

(3) The claimed spreadsheet behavior is unverified. Nothing was opened in a real spreadsheet. LibreOffice 24.2.7.2 core, writer, draw and impress are installed, but Calc is not: there is no libsclo.so and no libreoffice-calc package. I installed nothing. The Excel ';' list-separator claim rests only on Python's csv module standing in for Excel.

It is worth keeping as a low-priority AMO-03 hardening issue. Note that the proposed fix also changes the stored text: it inserts an apostrophe in the middle of the title.

verdicts.reason: I reproduced the behaviour, but it matches the documented policy and is not a rollback attack. My script (r10_versions.py, throwaway keys) installs 2027.03.01, then 2027.04.01, then rolls back to 03.01. A validly signed 2027.03.15 is then installed. Before the rollback, the same 03.15 was refused. install_bundle compares the new version with the installed (current) one (bundle.py:235-238), which is exactly what the guide specifies and tests. jaiden.md says 'A version that is not newer is refused, so an old signed bundle cannot be replayed to roll the rules back; rollback is the deliberate way back', and the CLI message reads 'not newer than the installed'. After the replay, the active rules (03.15) are newer than what the operator had chosen (03.01). So an attacker cannot lower the running version, and the case only arises after the owner's own rollback. The operator can still re-install 04.01: my run shows 'install 2027.04.01: INSTALLED'. Removing 04.01 from versions/ is normal retention (keep current and previous). Recording the highest version ever installed (TUF-style) is a stricter policy the team could choose, but it is a design choice, not a defect. Note that the proposed patch also refuses re-installing 04.01 after a rollback.
